_meta.purpose: MISC Starlancer MAX ship + zone definitions.
_meta.axis_convention: Width = port-to-starboard (X). Length = ramp-end to forward (Y). Height = floor up (Z). All units are 1.25 m cubes; scu_capacity = width x length x height.
_meta.ramp_note: The Starlancer MAX loads via the rear; both bays use ramp_side='low_y' with ship_forward_y='high' so the rear/entry end renders at the bottom of the diagram.
_meta.adjacency_note: left_zone_label / right_zone_label list zones that are physically open to each other so a wide load can span them. No zones on the Starlancer MAX connect laterally — every column is walled/walkway-separated — so all adjacency fields are null.
_meta.layout_note: Forward bay = two columns F1/F2 (2 x 16 x 2 = 64 SCU each). Rear bay = side columns R1/R2 (2 x 8 x 3 = 48 SCU each) flanking the central bulk floor, which is split into RB (the main 4 x 10 x 2 = 80 SCU body) and RBS (the 4 x 1 x 2 = 8 SCU strip at the rear ramp edge).
_meta.rb_split_note: The rear bulk floor is split into two zones instead of a single 4 x 11 x 2 = 88 rectangle: RB (4 x 10 x 2 = 80 SCU) fits exactly 10 standard 8-SCU pads with no leftover, and RBS (4 x 1 x 2 = 8 SCU) is the awkward last row that only fits small pallets (1 or 2 SCU). Together they keep the in-game 88 SCU rating without the 'odd 11th pad' packing artifact that left RB blank in the Zone Detail view when fully loaded. Both zones get higher unload_priority than F/R columns so the planner treats them as last-resort overflow (RB before RBS, since RB is the larger and easier-to-load chunk).
_meta.totals: Ship total = F1 64 + F2 64 + R1 48 + R2 48 + RB 80 + RBS 8 = 312 SCU.

zones.notes: Forward bay, port column. 2 x 16 x 2 = 64 SCU.
Forward bay, starboard column. 2 x 16 x 2 = 64 SCU.
Rear bay, port column. 2 x 8 x 3 = 48 SCU.

Rear Bulk Strip — the 4 x 1 x 2 = 8 SCU row at the rear ramp edge. Footprint is too shallow for a standard 8-SCU pad (which needs 2x2), so this zone only ever accepts 1 or 2 SCU smalls. Last-resort priority below RB.

Rear Bulk — the vehicle-bay floor used for bulk cargo. 4 x 10 x 2 = 80 SCU. Fits exactly 10 standard 8-SCU pads (2 across x 5 along) with no leftover — packs cleanly every time. Last-resort priority above the F/R columns so the planner only fills it when smaller bays are full.
Rear bay, starboard column. 2 x 8 x 3 = 48 SCU.
